user.title: Which sensors measure what?
user.description: Solar Sanity checks that your energy figures add up, so it needs to know which sensor is which. Fields are pre-filled from your Energy Dashboard where possible — {found} were found. Consumption and generation are both required: without consumption the arithmetic closes by definition and cannot tell you anything.

data_description.pv: Power or energy produced by your panels.
data_description.grid_import: Power or energy drawn from the grid. If you have one sensor that goes negative when exporting, put it here and leave export empty.
data_description.grid_export: Power or energy sent to the grid.
data_description.battery_discharge: Energy coming out of the battery.

topology.title: A few things only you know
topology.description: Everything else is worked out from your data. Answer "Not sure" for anything you are unsure of — it is a real answer, and Solar Sanity will infer it rather than assume.

data.has_battery: Do you have a home battery?
data.grid_is_net: Is your grid connection one sensor that goes negative when exporting?
data.load_whole_house: Does your consumption sensor cover the whole house?
data.forecast_entries: Solar forecast integrations to keep history for

data_description.load_whole_house: Answer "No" if it only covers a backup or critical-loads panel.
data_description.forecast_entries: Home Assistant discards yesterday's forecast, so Solar Sanity records it as it is issued. Pick any forecast integrations you already have.

reconfigure.title: Change which sensors are used
reconfigure.description: Correct a mapping without losing any history.

error.load_required: A consumption sensor is required. Without one the balance closes by definition and Solar Sanity cannot check anything.
error.duplicate_entity: The same sensor is mapped to two different roles. One sensor cannot be on both sides of the calculation — it would cancel itself out.

abort.already_configured: These sensors are already being monitored.
abort.unique_id_mismatch: These sensors belong to a different installation.

data_description.guaranteed_annual_kwh: The yearly figure your installer promised, if you have it. Solar Sanity will track your actual production against it, corrected for how sunny each year actually was.
